CHIEF COMPLAINT
Rash with residual lesions despite treatment.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a Fitzpatrick skin type IV female with perioral dermatitis and rosacea, including ocular rosacea. She reports her condition has improved significantly but notes a small amount of rash remains, primarily on bilateral medial cheeks and around the nostrils. She was initially taking doxycycline twice daily and noted substantial improvement. Approximately one week ago, she reduced the doxycycline to once daily based on pharmacist recommendation, but reports the rash has plateaued and is not continuing to improve. She denies current breastfeeding. She attempted to use only doxycycline initially because she had concerns about elidel after reading about its risks, though she now understands those concerns primarily relate to oral high-dose long-term use post-transplant. She is currently using sulfacetamide wash twice daily and metro cream after face washing, with no other skincare products. The sulfacetamide wash is not causing excessive dryness.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports feeling sun-sensitive when outdoors and takes sun protection precautions including wearing a hat. Denies dryness or thinning of facial skin.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Perioral dermatitis
Rosacea, including ocular rosacea

MEDICATIONS
Doxycycline 100 mg once daily (recently reduced; previously twice daily)
Sulfacetamide wash twice daily
Metro cream (metronidazole) applied twice daily after face washing

ALLERGIES
Not documented in this visit.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not addressed in this visit.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is not currently breastfeeding.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Fitzpatrick skin type IV. Bilateral medial cheeks with a few faint erythematous papules. Minimal erythema around and underneath nostrils. Overall improvement from previous exam but residual lesions present.

RESULTS
Not applicable.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Perioral dermatitis and rosacea, including ocular rosacea, with residual lesions showing plateau in improvement after dose reduction.

Plan:
1. Increase doxycycline back to twice daily until rash is completely resolved, then continue once daily for an additional week before stopping. Discussed potential side effects including upset stomach, heartburn, and photosensitivity requiring sun protection.
2. Initiate tacrolimus ointment (calcineurin inhibitor, non-steroid) to be applied twice daily to affected areas until rash resolves. Patient counseled that brief transient tingly sensation may occur but is not an allergic reaction. Discussed that this medication does not cause skin thinning and is not a steroid.
3. Continue sulfacetamide wash; discussed reducing to once daily to minimize dryness, but patient may use twice daily if tolerated well.
4. Continue metronidazole cream twice daily.
5. Avoid steroid use on face as it may worsen this type of rash and cause skin thinning.
6. Add moisturizer such as Vanicream or petroleum jelly as needed for dryness.
7. Cancelled elidel cream prescription to simplify medication list.
8. Cancelled clindamycin from medication list.
9. Patient provided samples of moisturizer.
10. Advised to avoid anti-aging products and plant-based products; instructed to discuss any new products with provider before use.
11. Gently wash eyelids once daily with gentle cleanser such as Vanicream.
12. Use Bruder mask as needed for ocular rosacea.
13. If rash begins to flare mildly after clearing, may attempt tacrolimus alone for a few days; if inadequate, restart doxycycline.
14. If rash worsens rather than improves, patient should call or send MyChart message.
15. Follow-up visit scheduled for approximately 4 weeks.
16. Patient has adequate refills of doxycycline and sufficient metro cream and face wash on hand.
